arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: Mr. Mann argued the plain language of Exemption 2 dictates a narrow category.
He stated this category relates solely to internal personnel policies and rules.
Justice Alito highlighted the long-standing reliance on the Crooker decision.
Justice Sotomayor questioned the meaning of Congress limiting the amendment to Exemption 7.

sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: This case tests the scope of Exemption 2 under the Freedom of Information Act. the side that brought the case Milner seeks records. The Department of the Navy withholds them. The core issue is the definition of internal personnel rules.

sources.label: Official Supreme Court Transcript — file page 3, lines 20-40

sections.heading: How the case got here
paragraphs: The Supreme Court heard oral argument in this case on December 1, 2010.

sources.label: Official Supreme Court Transcript — file page 3, lines 8-18

sections.heading: What each side wants
paragraphs: Milner wants the Court to limit Exemption 2 to internal personnel rules.
The Navy wants the Court to maintain the broad Crooker interpretation.

sources.label: Official Supreme Court Transcript — file page 3, lines 20-40

sections.heading: What each side says
paragraphs: Milner argues the plain language of Exemption 2 dictates a narrow category.
The Navy argues Crooker remains the leading decision and commands reliance.

sources.label: Official Supreme Court Transcript — file page 3, lines 20-40

sections.heading: What the justices asked
paragraphs: Justice Breyer asked why the argument does not show acceptance of Crooker.
Justice Alito noted greater security concerns since 1981 regarding information disclosure.

sections.heading: Why it matters
paragraphs: The outcome defines the scope of FOIA exemptions. It determines which internal agency records remain confidential. It affects public access to government information. It clarifies the relationship between Exemption 2 and Exemption 7.
